paragraphs.paragraph_en: Recovering missing sensor observations is essential for reliable downstream monitoring in industrial and clinical time series. While diffusion-based imputation models generate plausible trajectories under random missingness, they suffer from high sampling latency and lose global periodic coherence when entire sensor blocks drop out consecutively. We present FlowImp, a conditional flow-matching framework that reconstructs contiguous missing blocks in three ODE solver steps. Specifically, FlowImp anchors straight transport paths on observed spectral priors and enforces cross-channel phase consistency via a lightweight Fourier regularizer. Across six multivariate benchmarks under 50% block missingness, FlowImp reduces imputation MAE by 19.3% compared with CSDI while accelerating inference by 24x.

paragraphs.paragraph_en: Recent deep forecasters have substantially reduced long-horizon error by replacing point-wise attention with sub-series patch tokenization and frequency-domain decomposition. These architectures effectively capture recurring seasonal patterns when training and test sequences share stationary statistical moments. Yet they implicitly assume that inter-channel correlations and spectral energy distributions remain time-invariant across the prediction window. When external shocks alter underlying system dynamics, this stationarity assumption collapses, causing frozen spectral filters to project outdated trends.

paragraphs.paragraph_en: Bridging non-stationary robustness and amplitude fidelity remains a core bottleneck in long-horizon forecasting. While instance normalization strips time-varying mean and variance shifts to stabilize attention weights, it simultaneously erases physical scale cues required to predict extreme load peaks. Conversely, retaining raw unnormalized inputs exposes self-attention layers to severe covariate shift, causing validation error to diverge over extended horizons. Resolving this tension requires a mechanism that disentangles intrinsic temporal dynamics from transient scale drift without discarding magnitude information.

paragraphs.paragraph_en: Instantiating closed-loop visuomotor diffusion on physical robots entails two technical challenges. First, because raw depth camera streams contain occlusion artifacts around reflective object edges, we introduce a tactile-guided cross-attention gate that reweights visual tokens upon contact onset. Second, to eliminate the 200 ms sampling bottleneck of iterative denoising, we formulate a trajectory consistency distillation objective that maps Gaussian noise directly to collision-free action chunks in two forward steps. Together, these designs sustain 50 Hz reactive control under partial visual occlusion.

paragraphs.paragraph_en: We evaluate DyTS-Net across eight long-horizon forecasting benchmarks and a real-world wind-turbine telemetry system spanning 1,400 sensors. Across all prediction horizons up to 720 steps, DyTS-Net reduces MSE by 12.8% over PatchTST and 17.4% over iTransformer, with the largest gains emerging during sudden weather-front transitions. Furthermore, our architecture requires 45% fewer FLOPs than full channel-mixing Transformers and transfers zero-shot to newly deployed turbine units without fine-tuning.

paragraphs.paragraph_en: Figure 2 illustrates the overall architecture of DyTS-Net, which maps raw sensor streams to multi-horizon forecasts through three sequential stages. Given an input sequence $\mathbf{X}$, the Adaptive De-stationary Tokenizer first separates local trend-scale statistics from normalized sub-series patches $\mathbf{Z}_0$. These normalized patches then pass through stacked Spectral-Spatial Mixing blocks, which jointly filter high-frequency channel noise in the Fourier domain and propagate cross-sensor phase dependencies via a sparse directed graph. Finally, the Scale-Guided Decoder fuses the refined structural representations with the projected neural-ODE scale trajectory to reconstruct the multi-horizon output $\hat{\mathbf{Y}}$.

paragraphs.paragraph_intent_zh: 我这一段想专门阐述时间序列模型中“如何在频域捕获全局周期性，同时在时域保留局部突发异常（Transient Anomalies）”的双分支耦合机制。
paragraphs.cohesion_formula: Time-Frequency Dilemma -> Spectral Global Branch -> Temporal Local Branch -> Uncertainty-Gated Fusion. 绑定逻辑规则：L023, L024.
paragraphs.paragraph_en: Modeling telemetry streams solely in the time domain struggles to span multi-day periodicities, whereas pure Fourier projection spreads localized transient spikes across the entire spectrum. To reconcile both scales, our dual-domain block processes input patches along two complementary pathways. The spectral pathway applies real-valued RFFT to isolate top-$k$ harmonic bases governing macro-periodicity, while the parallel temporal pathway employs dilated depthwise convolutions to retain sharp step changes and localized anomalies. An energy-ratio gate then fuses both representations at each time step, dynamically shifting weight toward the temporal pathway whenever local high-frequency residual energy spikes.

paragraphs.paragraph_en: Table 1 reports the multivariate forecasting results, where DyTS-Net secures the lowest error in 25 out of 28 dataset-horizon configurations. Compared with channel-independent PatchTST, DyTS-Net reduces average MSE by 14.2% on the 862-channel Traffic benchmark, where modeling spatial-temporal congestion propagation across adjacent road sensors is critical. Furthermore, while variate-mixing iTransformer performs competitively at $H=96$, its MSE escalates by 68% at $H=720$ on volatile Weather series as unregularized cross-channel attention overfits transient wind gusts. By decoupling stationary phase coupling from neural-ODE scale projection, DyTS-Net suppresses long-horizon drift and maintains an 11.6% margin over the strongest baseline at $H=720$.

Removing the neural-ODE scale tracker (w/o Scale-ODE) triggers the sharpest degradation during seasonal transition months on ETTm2, raising 720-step MSE by 19.4% as the decoder fails to track shifting baseline temperatures. paragraphs.paragraph_en: In this work, we resolved the long-standing tension between shift-invariant normalization and physical amplitude preservation in non-stationary time series forecasting. By decoupling frequency-domain phase attention from continuous neural-ODE scale tracking, DyTS-Net captures long-range seasonal dependencies while accurately reconstructing extreme peak magnitudes. Empirical evaluations across eight benchmarks and industrial wind-power telemetry demonstrated MSE reductions of up to 17.4% alongside a 45% reduction in computational overhead. Beyond forecasting, this structural-scale disentanglement principle provides a generalizable foundation for anomaly detection and closed-loop predictive control in non-stationary cyber-physical systems.
